name: line-bot-sdk-python-cc640a73-blind30-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing a faulted line-bot-sdk-python checkout without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

A program built on this library talks to a chat service: it composes what gets sent to people, asks the service for counts and breakdowns about them, and reads the notices the service posts back. All three now go wrong in many places. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the calling code changed; the same work that used to succeed now fails, and in most cases it fails loudly rather than quietly.

Composing something to send is where most of it shows up, and much of it fails the instant a piece of the message is created rather than when it goes out. Tagging a user inside a text message blows up as soon as the tag is built, and so does attaching the small inline pictogram annotations that decorate a text message; both die with the same shape of type error, complaining that the first argument handed to the parent-class lookup is not a class. The prebuilt two-button yes/no layout cannot be constructed at all for the same reason, so every script that prepares one alongside its carousel and picture-carousel siblings never gets as far as sending anything. Narrowing an audience by geographic region fails the same way, as does aiming a send at the people reached by an earlier call id, while the rules beside them for age, gender, device type and how long someone has been receiving messages build fine.
